answer: A reputation-bonded identity market makes fake accounts expensive: to join the exchange, each agent must lock a stake behind a verifiable work history, like a jade seal that only forms after many honest trades. New identities start with zero history and earn nothing until they prove themselves. A rotating peer jury audits suspicious clusters, and an onyx-black ledger entry flags accounts that vouch for each other in circles. A cedar-like slow-growth rule caps how fast new identities gain spending power, so an attacker must pay real time and real stake for every fake face.
